verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe isolated cloud browser sessions that you control programmatically, each with a CDP WebSocket endpoint, which covers programmatic session management. Concurrency is only evidenced by a community remark that Hyperbrowser's pricing offers more concurrency than Browserbase, which implies tiered concurrency limits but does not document them. Missing for 10: first-party documented concurrency limits per plan, documented session list/stop/lifecycle management APIs, and hands-on evidence of running a concurrent fleet at scale.

support.subject: As an automation-engineer, I can run a fleet of concurrent browser sessions with documented concurrency limits and programmatic session management

citations.quote: Sessions are isolated browser instances running in the cloud that you can control programmatically.
Control Chrome browsers in the cloud using Puppeteer, Playwright, or our SDKs—no infrastructure management required.
you give twice as much concurrency/browsing/data-transfer as Browserbase
